# Didache Chapter 16 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Hierosolymitanus (H), Didache 16 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/DID_016_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 16

**1** Watch over your life. Do not let your lamps go out or your belts be loosened, but be ready — for you do not know the hour when our Lord is coming.

**2** Come together frequently, seeking what is beneficial for your souls. For all the time of your faith will not profit you unless you are made perfect at the very end.

**3** For in the last days false prophets and corruptors will be multiplied, and the sheep will be turned into wolves, and love will be turned into hate.

**4** As lawlessness increases, people will hate and persecute and betray one another, and then the world-deceiver will appear as a son of God. He will perform signs and wonders, the earth will be handed over into his hands, and he will do lawless deeds such as have never occurred since the world began.

**5** Then the human race will come into the fire of testing, and many will fall away and perish. But those who hold fast in their faith will be saved by the Accursed One himself.

**6** And then the signs of the truth will appear: first, the sign of an opening in heaven; then, the sign of the sound of a trumpet; and third, the resurrection of the dead —

**7** not the resurrection of all, but as it was said: "The Lord shall come, and all his holy ones with him."

**8** Then the world will see the Lord coming on the clouds of heaven.

---

*LOGOS notes: Ch. 16 is the eschatological climax of the Didache, drawing heavily on the Synoptic Apocalypse (Matt 24-25; Mk 13) and the prophetic tradition (Zech 14:5; Dan 7:13). V.5's "saved by the Accursed One himself" (ὑπ᾽ αὐτῆς τῆς κατάρας) is the most debated phrase in the text. One reading: "the Curse" = Christ, who became a curse on our behalf (Gal 3:13; Deut 21:23). LOGOS renders "the Accursed One himself" as the most coherent reading in context — the paradox of salvation through the one who bore the curse. V.7 cites Zech 14:5 with "his holy ones" — may include both angels and departed saints (cf. 1 Thess 3:13; 4:14).*
